column1: # Edges of the rules OpenVerse took from Epic's verdicts on followup-book2 (#724), compile-first probes: what OpenVerse does is in each probe's header and in note (Lean and C agreeing); Epic's outcome in epic_outcome: UEFN 43.12, ++Fortnite+Release-43.12-CL-60598086, each compiled alone with BuildAll on 2026-11-19 (~16:45Z; raw records compile-book3.json; L the diagnostic's 0-based body line as compiled, startLine - 10); compile only, not run. 13 matched OpenVerse at 71a08487, 9 did not: case-collision-classes, case-collision-interface, array-named-pack, parametric-var-where-nested and five long-ident probes; OpenVerse follows all 22 since (#724). Below the probes, Epic's bisection of the name-length limits (compile only, the same build and day), which the length rules take. Run the long-ident probes alone (single mode).

column7: note

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): refused, 3509 L9 "This function parameter expects a value of type tuple([]int,?B:int = ...), but this argument is an incompatible value of type tuple(type{1},type{2})." (1 diagnostics). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the 3509 rule (#724): F(1, 2) of F(A:[]int, ?B:int = 2), several arguments for an array parameter beside a named one. OpenVerse still makes the arguments an array, and prints result 4 If Epic refuses it (3509), an array parameter beside a named one takes no several arguments either. OpenVerse now (#724, this branch): refused, as Epic: "F takes 1 positional argument(s), found 2: several arguments do not make an array parameter beside a named one, since the function's parameter is then".

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): refused, 9002 L7 "Found existing type 'CC' that is already being created this compile. Please rename the class to be case insensitive unique." (1 diagnostics). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): two classes, cc and CC. The rule OpenVerse takes is the functions'; it admits two classes and prints lower 1 | upper 2 If Epic refuses it (9002, an existing type?), classes collide too. OpenVerse now (#724, this branch): refused, as Epic: "the types cc and CC have names that differ only in case: Epic's toolchain makes the two one, its names being case-insensitive, so rename one (Epic's V".

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): admitted (compiled only). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): a function Function() and a constant FUNCTION. OpenVerse admits them and prints lower 42 | upper 420 If Epic refuses it, a constant and a function collide too.

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): admitted (compiled only). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): a method Function() and, in a subclass, FUNCTION(). The Book has the case commented out (FORT-793952...:346, "TODO(SOL-9082)", 9200). OpenVerse measures one class's own methods only, and prints lower 42 | upper 420 If Epic refuses it, a subclass's methods count with its parents'.

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): refused, 9200 L7 "Found multiple functions that map to the same target function. Please rename the function to be case insensitive unique. See:" (1 diagnostics). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): an interface's two methods with defaults, Function() and FUNCTION(), and a class that inherits both. OpenVerse does not measure an interface's methods, and prints lower 42 | upper 420 If Epic refuses it, an interface's methods collide as a class's do. OpenVerse now (#724, this branch): refused, as Epic: "Function and FUNCTION, of ii, have names that differ only in case and take the same parameters: Epic's toolchain maps the two to one function, its nam".

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): admitted (compiled only). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): Function(X:int) beside FUNCTION(?X:int = 420), one positional, one named. OpenVerse tells them apart (a named parameter by its name) and prints lower 42 | upper 420 If Epic refuses it (9200 or 9000), a named parameter does not tell them apart.

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): refused, 9000 L8 "Local variable `A` not found internally in VM." (2 diagnostics). OpenVerse: refused. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): two functions whose names differ only in case, with one parameter type, int, under other names (A, B). Epic refuses Function(Value:int) beside FUNCTION(Value:int), 9000 (followup-book2/case-collision-same-params); does a parameter's name tell them apart? OpenVerse compares the types only, and refuses it ("have names that differ only in case and take the same parameters"). If Epic admits it, it prints lower 42 | upper 420

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): admitted (compiled only). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the interface-implementation rule (#724): class_z := class(class_x, i_y) {}, with class_x's MethodX() = 1 and i_y's MethodX() = 3, a default this time. Epic refuses it when i_y's MethodX is abstract (3591, followup-book2/final-method-interface-nonfinal). OpenVerse admits it and, as in Java, takes the class chain's method for i_y's slot: through the interface 1 If Epic takes the interface's default: through the interface 3; it may also refuse it as ambiguous.

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): refused, 3655 L8 "Identifier is too long" (1 diagnostics). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the name-length rules (#724): a class of 1023 characters. Epic refuses one of 1024 (9002) and runs one of 960. OpenVerse admits names of a class up to 1023 characters and prints field 42 | method 1 If Epic refuses it, the class limit is lower (a prefix or suffix in its internal name). Run it alone (single mode). OpenVerse now (#724, this branch): refused, as Epic: "the method F… of Class___…: their names have 1024 characters together, more than 987, the most Epic's compiler takes for a method's (UEFN 43.12, measu".

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): refused, 3655 L6 "Identifier is too long" (4 diagnostics). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the identifier limit (#724): a field of exactly 1024 characters. Epic refuses 1025 (3655) and let a class's name of 1024 pass that check (to fail with 9002). OpenVerse admits it and prints field 42 Run it alone (single mode). OpenVerse now (#724, this branch): refused, as Epic: "the name of a field, VarXAbcd…, has 1024 characters, more than 1004, the most Epic's compiler takes there (UEFN 43.12, measured for definitions withou".

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): refused, 3655 L6 "Identifier is too long" (1 diagnostics). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the identifier limit (#724): a module function of exactly 1024 characters; the Blueprint VM's names hold 1023, as for a class (9002 at 1024). OpenVerse admits it and prints result 42 If Epic refuses it, a function's name is limited as a class's is. Run it alone (single mode). OpenVerse now (#724, this branch): refused, as Epic: "the name of a function, FunXAbcd…, has 1024 characters, more than 990, the most Epic's compiler takes there (UEFN 43.12, measured for definitions with".

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): admitted (compiled only). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the mangled-name limit (#724): a class of 976 characters with a method Function() without parameters (the refused long-ident-mangled has Function(Param:int)). OpenVerse prints field 42 | method 1 If Epic refuses it, the parameters are not what makes the mangled name too long. Run it alone (single mode).

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): refused, 3655 L9 "Identifier is too long" (1 diagnostics). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the mangled-name limit (#724): a class of 1000 characters with a method F(). Epic refuses Function(Param:int) in a class of 976 (3655, followup-book2/long-ident-mangled) and admits F() in one of 960. OpenVerse does not check a method's mangled name, and prints field 42 | method 1 If Epic refuses it, the limit counts the class's name and the method's, whatever its parameters. Run it alone (single mode). OpenVerse now (#724, this branch): refused, as Epic: "the method F… of Class___…: their names have 1001 characters together, more than 987, the most Epic's compiler takes for a method's (UEFN 43.12, measu".

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): refused, 9002 L4 "Cannot find struct: `Struct__`." (1 diagnostics). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the class-name limit (#724): a struct of 1024 characters (a class of 1024 is refused, 9002). OpenVerse limits classes only, and prints field 42 Run it alone (single mode). OpenVerse now (#724, this branch): refused, as Epic: "the struct name Struct__… has 1024 characters, more than 1023 (Epic's Verse compiler, UEFN 43.12: error 9002, "Cannot find struct")".

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): admitted (compiled only). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the 3552 rule (#724): c(t) has a var field that does not mention t (var Count:int) and an immutable Data:t; F(X:t where t:type):c(t). OpenVerse admits it and prints count 2 If Epic refuses it, any var field of a parametric class counts.

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): admitted (compiled only). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the 3552 rule (#724): a generic function constructs c(t) (with var Data:t) in its body, its type mentions no c. OpenVerse admits it and prints result 1 If Epic refuses it, the rule is not only about a function's type.

Epic (2026-11-19 ~16:45Z): refused, 3552 L12 "An implicit type parameter (`t`) used in the type of mutable data (`<project>/c.Data`) may not be used in the type of a function." (1 diagnostics). OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the 3552 rule (#724): holder(t) has an immutable field of c(t), whose var Data:t is mutable data; F(X:t where t:type):holder(t). OpenVerse measures a class's own var fields only, and prints data 2 If Epic refuses it (3552), the rule reaches mutable data through other types' fields. OpenVerse now (#724, this branch): refused, as Epic: "F's type has holder(…) at its implicit type parameter t, which mutable data holds, c.Data: an implicit type parameter used in the type of mutable data".
